ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Under Article 14 of Ley 10/2010, mandatory enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates. Screening must cover the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU terrorist financing lists (Council Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001), and Spanish domestic sanctions and warnings published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales). The protocol requires identification of beneficial owners, verification from public or independent sources, and documenting higher-risk non-resident or non-EU structures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — Sede Electrónica del Colegio de Registradores de España (www.registradores.org); formal application for 'Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social' in the mercantile registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name of an SL must be written in Spanish or in an official co-official language of an autonomous community (Catalan, Basque, Galician, or Occitan/Aranese). Foreign-language words are admitted only where there is no equivalent acceptable in the Spanish language, or when they are proper names. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters using official Spanish transliteration rules. The name must be unique and not identical or phonetically or graphically so similar to an existing registered name so as to create confusion; accents are treated as insignificant for identity comparison.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España or Spanish-derived national terms without prior ministerial authorization
Cooperativa (unless the legal form is a cooperative registered under the corresponding special law)
Sociedad Anónima or SA where the entity is not such a company
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrador Mercantil Central denies a negative name certificate, the applicant may file a written appeal ('recurso de alzada') before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of notification, under the general administrative procedure of Ley 39/2015. The applicant may simultaneously request new name cases; if the certificate is rejected due to graphical/phonetic similarity, the appeal must state distinctive arguments and supply prior trademark or registry search results. Alternately, a re-application before the same registrar with a materially different name is acceptable and less costly.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable as the registered address for correspondence and administrative purposes, provided that it constitutes a genuine place of management with staff and working facilities. A bare mailbox or an address without actual services will be rejected during mercantile registration and by AEAT fiscal registration. For the low-risk die-struck hard enamel lapel pins e-commerce business, a licensed serviced-flexi office in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, or another provincial hub satisfies minimum substance requirements. AEAT may nevertheless require further evidence of a fixed establishment for VAT and corporate tax if significant management or economic activity occurs in Spain.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-modest (5% to 10% annual probability) for a low-risk e-commerce merchandising company. The likelihood rises above 20% where there are atypical VAT refunds, irregular B2C payment flows, or unresolved UBO transparency indicators.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); digital portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); official site: www.agenciatributaria.es. Local delegations of the AEAT handle SME compliance; the Delegación Central de Grandes Contribuyentes supervises large-taxpayer files.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SL public deed before a notary; the notary submits the provisional-NIF request and AEAT grants a provisional NIF beginning with the letter 'N' (entidad en constitución). Step 2: Inscribe the deed at the Mercantile Registry within the statutory registration period (2 months); inscription is a precondition for the definitive NIF. Step 3: Submit Modelo 036 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) through the AEAT Sede Electrónica before commencement of activity, declaring the SL status, ISIC 3240 manufacturing scope, registered address, non-resident shareholders, the appointed tax representative, and the applicable Corporation Tax, VAT, and withholding obligations. Step 4: After Registry confirmation, request the definitive NIF (format: letter 'B' for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, 8 digits, control character) via Modelo 036 data-amplification procedure. Step 5: Obtain an electronic certificate (CERES/FNMT entity certificate, or individual power of attorney) enabling authenticated filings, digital invoicing, and future SII or Verifactu exchanges. Step 6: Complete IVA registration (Modelo 036, general regime), IAE census (new activities benefit from municipal IAE exemption for 2 years), and, if employees are engaged, employer registration with the Seguridad Social. Step 7: Register non-resident shareholder dividend withholding obligations (Modelo 216 quarterly). Failure to register is an infracción tributaria grave under art. 199 LGT with fines of €200 per omitted data item plus late-filing penalties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SL is a Spanish-resident company taxed under Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014, LIS) on worldwide income, with a standard rate of 25% for 2024/2025 and a reduced 15% rate for the first taxable period with positive taxable income and the immediately following period in newly incorporated entities. The SL is not a pass-through: profits are subject to entity-level tax, and distributions to non-resident shareholders are exposed to 19% dividend withholding (treaty relief available); distributions to Spanish-resident individuals are taxed under the savings-income scale.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not recognise US-style check-the-box or flow-through passthrough elections for SL entities. Available statutory elections: (1) Optional consolidated tax group regime under art. 64 LIS, requiring ≥75% shareholding and aggregate group turnover ≥€2M; the individual SL remains the taxpayer unless the election is made. (2) Optional cash-basis VAT 'criterio de caja' under art. 163 decies LIVA, available when annual turnover does not exceed €2,000,000, deferring the VAT charge point to receipt of payment. (3) Optional Simplified VAT Regime (régimen simplificado) for listed minor industrial and retail activities with prior-year volume of operations ≤€250,000. (4) Optional depreciation elections: free choice of straight-line or declining-balance methods, accelerated depreciation for newly acquired tangible assets, and capitalisation or expense elections for intangibles. (5) ATAD anti-hybrid rules (arts. 15 ter and 15 quater LIS) and DAC6 disclosure obligations apply; no hybrid neutralisation of double non-taxation is permitted. (6) Alternative territorial regimes of Canary Islands (IGIC), Ceuta, and Melilla (IPSI) are not applicable to this unitary peninsular Spain file.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido / Value Added Tax) — governed by Ley 37/1992 and RD 1624/1992, harmonised with EU Directive 2006/112/EC. The SL must charge output VAT on peninsular Spanish supplies and intra-EU distance sales; input VAT on manufacturing inputs is recoverable through Modelo 303 declarations. Supplies to the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside peninsular VAT and are documented as exports when physically dispatched.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None general: every entrepreneur habitually supplying taxable goods or services in Spanish territory must obtain a NIF and register for VAT (Modelo 036) before starting the activity, regardless of turnover. Turnover thresholds apply only to optional special regimes: Simplified VAT Regime requires prior-year volume of operations ≤€250,000 (and the specific activity must be covered); Retail Surcharge Regime (Recargo de Equivalencia) applies only to non-manufacturing retailers with sales ≤€150,000; optional Cash-Basis Regime applies to taxpayers with volume of operations and annual deliveries ≤€2,000,000. A hard enamel lapel pin manufacturer (ISIC 3240) is normally in the general regime; the recargo de equivalencia is unavailable to production companies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: 1) Verifactu anti-fraud rules (RD 1007/2023): all commercial invoicing/ERP software must generate an integrity record with hash-chain and QR codes; newly integrated systems must comply from the 2024/2025 transition and all in-force software by 1 July 2025. 2) Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) is being phased by Royal Decree, requiring structured e-invoices (Facturae or equivalent APE/STPE formats) between businesses; SME phase currently in implementation. 3) Real-time fiscal clearance (SII — Suministro Inmediato de Información) is compulsory for taxpayers with invoiced turnover above €6,000,000 in the prior year, consolidated-group members, and VAT-group participants; it requires XML/SOAP API submission of invoice books within 4 calendar days of the record date; smaller exporters may opt in voluntarily. 4) B2G invoices to Spanish public entities must be submitted to the FACe platform in Facturae format. 5) No per-invoice digital stamping is required below the SII threshold, but the billing system must produce Verifactu audit records; Etsy/Stripe-settled online sales remain within the same invoicing integrity regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: exports of die-struck brass and cloisonné hard enamel lapel pins to non-EU destinations (including the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla) are zero-rated (exemption with credit) under art. 21 LIVA where the goods physically leave the EU customs territory within 3 months of delivery/dispatch, the SL is the exporter of record on the DUA, and transport documents evidence the exit. Etsy sales to non-EU consumers qualify when the SL issues the export declaration and retains the carrier chain; if Etsy or a 3PL handles logistics, the SL must evidence the contractual principal relationship. Services: zero-rating applies to transport and ancillary services directly connected to exported goods (art. 23 LIVA) and to B2B services supplied to non-EU business customers under the use-and-enjoyment rule (art. 69.2 LIVA); domestic merchandising services remain 21%. Intra-EU channel: B2B supplies to EU VAT-registered customers are exempt in Spain under art. 25 LIVA subject to VIES validation; B2C distance sales to other EU states remain Spanish-taxable up to the €10,000 union-wide threshold, and above that threshold (or upon election) must be declared through the OSS One-Stop-Shop, with VAT charged at the destination Member State.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA / SAD — Single Administrative Export Declaration naming the SL (definitive NIF) as exporter, bearing the applicable HS codes for ISIC 3240 products (e.g., HS 7117, 8306, 9617) and indicating the 0% IVA exemption under art. 21 LIVA.

Commercial invoice in the sale currency issued by the SL, identifying the non-EU buyer, Incoterms, quantity, unit price, and the 0% VAT block; invoice must be logged in the Libro de Facturas Expedidas.
Bill of Lading (maritime), Airway Bill (air), CMR (road), or courier customs manifest proving physical departure from EU customs territory within the 3-month window.
Customs exit confirmation — stamped DUA or Export Control System (ECS) result from AEAT customs issuing the 'justificante de exportación'.
Etsy Direct Pay payout reports and settlement statements identifying each non-EU buyer, marketplace fees, and net remitted amounts.
Stripe/PSP bank credit evidence and Inward Remittance Certificate or SMV (Servicio de Medios de Pago) certificate from the Spanish bank showing the EUR conversion and credit date.
Forwarding/3PL instruction documents and any insurance certificate supporting the transport chain when export logistics are outsourced.
For intra-EU B2B transactions: VIES validation output, kept separately from the non-EU export file.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits verify the DUA-transport-payment triangle. If the export cannot be substantiated (missing exit certificate, buyer/payment mismatch, proceeds not credited within 180 days, or invoice issued without customs backing), the 0% rate is reversed: the supply is recast as domestic at 21%, the VAT self-assessment is corrected via Modelo 303/390, and input VAT previously deducted on production costs is clawed back pro rata under art. 28 LIVA (regularización). Penalties: under arts. 191-192 LGT the infringement is grave — 50% to 100% of the omitted tax for non-fraudulent conduct and up to 150% for fraudulent concealment, plus late-payment interest (interés de demora); where the evaded amount exceeds €120,000, criminal tax fraud under art. 305 Código Penal applies (imprisonment of 1-5 years and fines). The tax-claim limitation period is 4 years (art. 66 LGT); exporters must keep the full evidentiary bundle for at least 4 years (10 years for SII-registered operators) and must produce requested documentation within 15 working days of an AEAT formal request under the invoicing-record rules, failing which immediate regularization may be issued.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange and payment-services rules also derive from European Union law, Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation, and reporting regulations administered through Banco de España and the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and has no general exchange controls. Current-account transactions, including imports, exports, service payments, dividends, interest, royalties, and ordinary profit remittances, are generally freely convertible and transferable within applicable tax, sanctions, AML, accounting, and documentation requirements. Capital-account transactions are also generally liberalized, although certain foreign direct investment transactions may require mandatory post-investment declarations or, in restricted strategic sectors, prior authorization. Profit distributions require distributable accounting profits, satisfaction of Spanish corporate-law reserves and solvency requirements, shareholder approval, and appropriate withholding-tax analysis. Dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents may be subject to Spanish withholding tax unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, or another statutory exemption. Banks may require invoices, board resolutions, financial statements, tax certificates, beneficial-owner information, and evidence of the underlying transaction before processing large or unusual transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to Banco de España, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general deadline requiring conversion of foreign-currency export receipts into euros. The Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may retain export proceeds in foreign-currency accounts or convert them commercially, subject to bank terms, accounting rules, tax reporting, sanctions screening, AML controls, and accurate recognition of foreign-currency transactions. Cross-border payment and balance-of-payments information may be reportable by the relevant financial institution or resident entity under applicable Spanish and European statistical-reporting rules. Export documentation, commercial invoices, customs records, transport evidence, and payment reconciliation should be retained for the statutory accounting and tax-preservation periods.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, euro operating accounts, card acquiring, and routine supplier payments, provided the provider is an EU-authorized electronic money institution or payment institution passported into Spain. An offshore digital EMI without EU authorization or a valid EEA passport cannot lawfully provide regulated payment-account, payment-initiation, acquiring, or money-remittance services to the Spanish SL merely through an online interface. Fintech balances may not provide the same deposit-guarantee protection as bank deposits. Providers may restrict marketplace proceeds, high-volume card receipts, chargeback exposure, sanctioned jurisdictions, cash activity, and transfers involving unrelated third parties. The SL should maintain a Spanish or EEA bank account as its primary treasury and contingency account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available using qualified electronic identification, video identification, electronic signatures, and certified corporate documentation, subject to the bank's risk policy. Banks may require an in-person meeting where the shareholder chain is complex, a director or ultimate beneficial owner is non-resident, documents are issued outside the EEA, the business has elevated payment or marketplace risk, source-of-funds evidence is incomplete, or automated identification fails. The bank may require identification and verification of directors, authorized signatories, direct and indirect beneficial owners, controlling persons, and persons exercising management control. A notarial power of attorney can assist with local representation but does not eliminate ultimate-beneficial-owner verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, opaque holding chains, nominee shareholders, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified incorporation documents for every relevant entity; current commercial-register extracts; complete ownership chart to the natural-person beneficial owners; passports and proof of address; director and authorized-signatory details; beneficial-owner declaration; shareholder agreements where relevant; notarized translations or apostilles when requested; and a written explanation of control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital or unexplained inbound transfers from shareholders, affiliates, or unrelated third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder resolutions; originating bank statements; audited or management financial statements of the funding entity; tax returns or tax-clearance evidence where available; sale-of-asset or dividend evidence for individual funders; SWIFT payment confirmation; and a funds-flow schedule matching the amount, sender, purpose, and accounting entry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce, Etsy, Stripe, marketplace, or payment-processor receipts that do not reconcile to the legal entity or stated business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant and marketplace agreements; processor onboarding approval; merchant-account ownership evidence; sales invoices and order reports; VAT records; payout statements; chargeback and refund policy; website and product catalogue; logistics records; customer-geography analysis; and monthly reconciliation from gross sales through fees, refunds, reserves, and net bank settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cross-border transfers, payments to high-risk jurisdictions, third-party payment instructions, or insufficient commercial purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due-diligence file; signed contracts; purchase orders; commercial invoices; customs declarations; bills of lading or courier records; service-delivery evidence; sanctions-screening records; payment-purpose matrix; approval controls; and written confirmation that beneficiary details were independently verified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive activity, inconsistent transaction volumes, rapid movement of funds, or transactions materially exceeding the business plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year or projected financial model; bankable business plan; sales-channel forecast; inventory and production records; supplier and customer concentration analysis; tax filings; management accounts; expected monthly transaction profile; treasury policy; and documented explanations for seasonal or exceptional peaks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-language, expired, uncertified, or inconsistent corporate and identity documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recently issued certified registry extracts; valid identity documents; proof of residential address; sworn or bank-accepted translations; apostilles or legalization where required; consistent transliteration of names; certificate of tax residence when relevant; and a document-validity tracker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions, politically exposed person exposure, adverse media, or an ownership connection to restricted territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening results; beneficial-owner and management questionnaires; source-of-wealth narrative; sanctions and export-control assessment; independent corporate-registry searches; adverse-media remediation memorandum; legal opinions where necessary; and documented enhanced-monitoring procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity or shareholder-loan funding from the verified shareholder's account directly to the SL's account through SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT for non-euro payments. Use an explicit payment narrative identifying the legal nature of the transfer, such as share capital contribution, share premium, or shareholder loan, and ensure the receiving bank's corporate records and accounting treatment match the payment. For a capital contribution connected with incorporation or a capital increase, coordinate the bank certificate, notarial deed, commercial-register filing, and corporate resolutions. For shareholder loans, maintain a signed loan agreement specifying principal, currency, maturity, interest, repayment terms, transfer-pricing support, and withholding-tax treatment. Confirm whether the transaction triggers Spanish foreign-investment reporting, statistical reporting, or related-party documentation. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated group entities, payment processors, or third-party collection accounts unless fully documented and accepted by the bank. Retain SWIFT MT103 or SEPA confirmation, source-of-funds evidence, and the complete funds-flow reconciliation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro supplier payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. For ordinary merchandise purchases, support each payment with an approved purchase order, commercial invoice, supplier due diligence, shipping or customs evidence where available, and a three-way match between purchase order, goods receipt, and invoice. For larger, new, or higher-risk suppliers, use an irrevocable documentary Commercial Letter of Credit governed by UCP 600, with documentary requirements aligned to the sale contract and transport terms. Banks may also support documentary collections under URC 522, bank guarantees, and standby letters of credit subject to credit approval. Verify beneficiary account details through an independent channel and apply dual authorization, sanctions screening, segregation of duties, payment limits, and post-payment reconciliation. Payment messages must accurately state the commercial purpose; Spain does not use a general mandatory FX purpose-code regime comparable to controlled-currency jurisdictions, but banks may request internal purpose classifications and supporting documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or regulated investment firm, documented against forecast or committed receivables and payables and subject to appropriateness, suitability, collateral, and accounting requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies that are not freely deliverable, where offered by an authorized counterparty and legally permitted for the entity, with cash settlement and documented underlying exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for managing recurring currency or funding exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, valuation controls, and EMIR obligations where applicable.

Foreign-exchange options, collars, and other permitted derivatives may be used with an authorized counterparty when the SL has sufficient treasury governance, understands premium and contingent-liability risks, and documents the underlying exposure.

Spot foreign-exchange conversion through the relationship bank or an appropriately authorized payment provider for ordinary operating settlements; speculative trading unrelated to the SL's commercial exposures should be prohibited by treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 days after the end of the tax year (typically June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 5% of the tax due per month of delay, up to a maximum of 150%; possible administrative fines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (Memoria Anual) with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after approval of the annual accounts (typically by June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from 300 to 6,000 euros for late filing; potential administrative strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation and update by June 30 or within 1 month of changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative sanctions and possible deletion from the beneficial ownership register

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Net turnover exceeding 2 million euros or total assets exceeding 1 million euros in the prior fiscal year
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General Contable)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual update of beneficial ownership details in the Registro Mercantil within one month of any change

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 0-500 USD (own premises or registered agent service)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (general corporate income tax rate for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada under Article 29.1 Ley 27/2014)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created SLs during the first two eligible taxable years with a positive taxable base, subject to Article 29 LIS thresholds; 60% patent box exemption for qualifying intangible property; 100% R&D and innovation deductions for qualifying expenditure; R&D personnel wage credit; double-taxation relief under unilateral or treaty credit rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 - Impuesto sobre Sociedades; filed electronically through the Agencia Tributaria Sede Electrónica (www.sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) using a recognised digital certificate, Cl@ve PIN, or authorised representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return under Modelo 200, with quarterly installment payments under Modelo 202/222 due in April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year entity, the annual Modelo 200 must be filed between 1 and 25 July following the fiscal year-end, i.e., within 25 calendar days after six months from the close of the tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before tax (resultado contable), as adjusted by the taxpayer for Spanish GAAP compliance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entity-level resident filing; non-resident shareholders do not complete this field and must report their Spanish-source income on the relevant non-resident form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of permanent and temporary differences (diferencias permanentes y temporales), including exempt dividend income, impairment charges, and nondeductible provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners claiming treaty or EU-Directive exemption must not include the company's internal tax adjustments in their personal non-resident computations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before loss compensation (base imponible antes de compensación de bases imponibles negativas).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the SL remain at entity level and cannot be transferred to non-resident shareholders; the foreign parent should compute its own Spanish-source income separately on Form 210.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses offset applied in the current period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Spanish resident SL may use the offset; non-resident shareholders cannot claim the company's tax losses for purposes of their own dividend WHT position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate tax liability at the applicable rate (25% standard; 15% reduced new-entity preference where eligible).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 19% non-resident dividend WHT is a separate, independent levy applied at distribution; it is not integrated into Box 00570/00572.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits, withholdings, and prepayments, resulting in the final differential tax payable or refundable (cuota diferencial).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder whose dividend WHT was over-withheld must claim a refund through the non-resident tax refund mechanism (Modelo 210/211), not through the resident SL's Modelo 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers graduated surcharges: 5% within three months, 10% from three to six months, 15% from six to twelve months, and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. In cases of non-filing after formal request or fraudulent reporting, proportional penalties range from 50% to 150% of the tax due; fixed penalties of EUR 200 to EUR 400 apply for untimely delivery of nil returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% general non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU parent entities and to applicable lower treaty rates where the shareholder is the beneficial owner and holds the relevant participation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain an official tax residence certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction and furnish it to the Spanish withholding agent before payment or, if withheld at 19%, within the statutory refund period. The payer or claimant files Form 210/211 to secure the reduced rate or refund; the beneficial owner must satisfy the anti-abuse, LOB, and substance provisions of the applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding is 19% on cross-border royalties and interest paid to non-residents. DTA-protocol rates generally reduce the rate to 0%-10%, and interest and royalties paid to associated EU companies may be exempt under Directive 2003/49/EC where economic substance and beneficial-ownership conditions are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 net turnover triggers mandatory Local File preparation; Master File obligations apply by reference to group consolidated turnover thresholds under Royal Decree 634/2015; Country-by-Country Report is required for groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations code. Equivalent enforcement flows from Article 15 LGT (general anti-abuse rule), Article 100 LIS (CFC rules), Article 107 LIS (hybrid mismatches), and the beneficial-ownership requirement embedded in every DTA and EU directive application. A Spanish SL claiming treaty or Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief must show personnel, premises, decision-making, risk management, and real commercial activity commensurate with the transactions; a hollow structure with no economic substance is a fatal compliance red flag.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Etsy or Stripe turnover from Modelo 200, use of unrecorded foreign bank accounts, or distortion of deductible costs through false supplier invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under Article 305 CP where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period: imprisonment for 2 to 6 years and a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded; administrative penalties of 50% to 150% of the under-declared tax plus late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under the levantamiento del velo doctrine; directors risk civil restitution, asset embargos, travel bans, disqualification from managing companies, and imprisonment when fraud is intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming and maintaining an SL without real staff, premises, business records, or operational activity solely to channel dividends, royalties, or intra-group payments through Spain for DTA/EU-Directive advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty and directive benefits, retroactive recharacterization of transactions, upward tax assessment, penalties of 50% to 150%, and revocation of beneficial-owner status; continued abuse may trigger a disciplinary strike-off or judicial dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly organize an artificial structure face joint and several liability under Article 42 LGT, reimbursement obligations for improperly obtained tax advantages, travel restrictions, and criminal exposure where the arrangement facilitates tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain Local File at the EUR 10,000,000 net turnover threshold, submission of false comparability documentation, or purchase/sale arrangements with related parties at prices materially departing from arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer-pricing correction plus a 15% transfer-pricing penalty on the adjusted amount under Article 18.13 LIS, late-payment interest, and proportional penalties (50%-150%) where the documentation is materially inaccurate or concealed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize fraudulent transfer-pricing documents can be derivatively liable for the resulting corporate tax debt, subject to criminal prosecution for accounting document falsification, and exposed to asset freezes, travel bans, and imprisonment up to four years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain accurate ultimate beneficial owner records under Law 10/2010, acceptance of unexplained cash payments linked to pin merchandise sales, or omission of suspicious transaction reports to SEPBLAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines range up to EUR 10,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for the most serious breaches; typical serious violations attract penalties from EUR 60,000 to EUR 1,500,000; criminal AML violations under Article 302 CP carry imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the obligated Spanish entity face criminal responsibility for wilful AML non-compliance, including imprisonment of one to three years, disqualification, travel bans, and confiscation of assets in aggravated cases.
